abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions track the app's real variation (cards, sections, badges, ref-to-species mapping) and an Items section would reuse nearly all of them via the established four-file recipe. Held back from 5 by the duplicated card construction and the optional-field creep on Card.

findings.issue: Card objects (id/name/label/sprite) are constructed identically in cardsFor (:146) and loadList (:172), so any change to card fields — e.g. deriving the sprite from the default Pokémon's record instead of the ID pattern — must be made twice or silently diverge.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared makeCard(species, extra?) helper used by both call sites.

findings.issue: spriteUrl fabricates sprite URLs from the species ID rather than using the API-provided sprites.front_default; per spec some sprite sets are null, and the pattern doesn't generalise to species whose default Pokémon differs.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the sprite from the default Pokémon's sprites.front_default (cardsFor already resolves species; fetch or cache the pokemon record) — done once in a shared card helper.

findings.issue: The generic Card DTO carries feature-specific optional fields (`hidden` for abilities, `types` for the home page), and PokemonCard renders 'Hidden ability' (ui.tsx:44), so the shared card component knows about one feature.
findings.suggestion: Keep Card minimal and pass feature annotations (types, hidden) as slot content or a small per-list wrapper.

findings.issue: The root head inspects match internals (`m._notFound || m.status === 'notFound'`) to compute the Not found title — a fragile, underscore-prefixed framework field.
findings.suggestion: Render the not-found title from the notFoundComponent's own route head, or rely on a per-route head fallback rather than match internals.

findings.issue: NotFound is registered twice: as the root route's notFoundComponent (__root.tsx:15) and as the router's defaultNotFoundComponent — redundant config that can drift.
findings.suggestion: Keep one registration (the root route's notFoundComponent is sufficient for a file-based route tree).

findings.issue: Validators are pass-through type assertions (`.validator((data: ListFilters) => data)`), so no runtime validation happens between client and server despite the validator plumbing.
findings.suggestion: Either validate for real (e.g. zod schema per input) or drop the validator where the loader already normalises input.

summary: This is a well-layered TanStack Start app: routes are thin, all server/API knowledge is quarantined in pokedex.server.ts behind server functions, and shared UI abstractions (CardList, Section, TypeBadge, Count) are genuinely reused across pages, so most changes land in one obvious place. The main editability cost is the duplicated Card construction in cardsFor and loadList, which is exactly where the likely sprite bug would have to be fixed twice. Feature-specific optional fields on the shared Card type add a small amount of cross-feature coupling.

No nav link and no ability-specific CSS exist, so nothing else is touched; routeTree.gen.ts regenerates on build. A thorough removal also unwinds Card.hidden, which spans three more files.

scenarios.change: Fix the wrong sprite for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: The sprite is derived from the ID pattern in spriteUrl (pokedex.server.ts:75), used at two card-construction sites (:146 cardsFor, :172 loadList) in the same file. A URL-pattern tweak in spriteUrl covers both, but a correct fix (use the default Pokémon's sprites.front_default, which can be null) requires fetching pokemon records in both sites and touching the Card type — doable, but duplicated logic means the change is made twice unless you first extract a shared card helper. Rendering is already centralised in PokemonCard, so no UI edits.
